actions.spoken: Meet MADHAV Order Desk: a simple way for small bakeries to turn customer messages into checked orders, with the owner in control.
Aanya asks in Hinglish for one chocolate cake tomorrow. Let's prepare the reply.
The sample parser identifies her product, quantity and pickup date for owner review. AMD live analysis is separately implemented, but not shown here.
The catalog—not the AI—sets the price at nine hundred rupees, with a suggested four hundred and fifty rupee advance.
Only my approval reserves the cake. Preparing the draft never books it.
I approve the reply separately. Here it appears in the demo chat; it's not a real WhatsApp send.
The order book now shows Aanya's nine hundred rupee order. No payment has been recorded.
Rohan wants Red Velvet. Let's check what happens when a product is sold out.
Capacity is zero. MADHAV blocks the booking and offers available alternatives. It never substitutes a product automatically.
Rohan chooses vanilla in a follow-up. The new customer message is fictional demo data.
We review the new proposal: one vanilla cake, seven hundred and fifty rupees.
Now I approve the vanilla order and its reply. Red Velvet remains unbooked.
Meera needs two cupcake boxes tomorrow.
The catalog price is four hundred and twenty per box. That's eight hundred and forty in total.
I reserve this order and approve the confirmation separately.
In Orders, we can see the full eight hundred and forty rupee total.
Now I manually record four hundred and twenty rupees received, after independent confirmation.
MADHAV shows four hundred and twenty paid, and four hundred and twenty still due. A payment claim never changes the ledger automatically.
AMD handles language understanding. Our code enforces prices, stock and owner approval. This is a chat simulation; official WhatsApp integration comes later. That's MADHAV.
